In roduc ion


Lunar dus coverage can significan ly impac he hermo-op ical proper ies of ex ernal surfaces for spacecraf and sys ems opera ing in he Lunar orbi or on he Lunar surface. This impac s he hermal con rol of hese vehicles. Tes ing mus be done o de ermine how much surface op ics are affec ed by varying levels of lunar dus coverage. Op ics and Par icle Size Dis ribu ions (PSDs) of he simulan used in hese es s are cri ical o he resul s [2]. Many lunar simulan s are available for es ing, bu heir hermo-op ical proper ies are no well charac erized. To resolve his unknown, 13 differen lunar dus simulan s’ IR emissivi y, ε, and solar absorp ivi y, α, were measured and are presen ed wi h heir PSDs here. Solar absorp ivi ies of lunar samples were calcula ed from reflec ance spec ra found in he Lunar Sourcebook and are compared o he measured absorp ivi ies of he simulan s. 





Op ics Measuremen Me hodology 


Simulan s were no ground, sieved, or o herwise processed. Samples were prepared for op ics measuremen by dispersing he par icles in isopropyl alcohol and hen dissolved in order o achieve a loose packed par icle bed in specially 3D prin ed sample con ainers. They were hen placed on a ho pla e o remove he mois ure resul ing in a fla , uniform hickness surface. Each con ainer was sealed wi h op ically ransparen low-densi y polye hylene before being placed in he spec rome ers o measure solar and IR ransmi ance and reflec ance, as shown in Figure 1. Solar op ics were measured in a Perkin Elmer Lambda 950 Spec rome er wi h a 150 mm in egra ing sphere and IR op ics were measured wi h a Thermo Scien ific Nicole iS50 wi h a midIn egra Sphere from Pike Technologies. Reflec ivi y and ransmissivi y da a were pos -processed using he AM0 solar spec rum o re urn α [1].

Conclusion


There was more varia ion in simulan α han ε. Lunar mare simulan s have a higher α han highlands simulan s, as is expec ed. Mare simulan s were sligh ly lower han he values calcula ed from published reflec ivi y of lunar Mare samples while highlands simulan s were generally sligh ly higher han highlands samples [3]. The IR ε of all simulan s were abou he same and had a s andard devia ion <0.01. I has been shown ha he smaller par icle sizes of lunar simulan s he higher he reflec ivi y [2]. In eres ingly, hese resul s canno suppor ha . The agglu ina e con en should also impac reflec ivi y [3]. OPRH3W simulan s indica e increased absorp ivi y wi h decreasing agglu ina e con en , con rary o NU LHT samples. More op ics measuremen s are needed where PSDs are equalized before es ing.
